Modern.brandNameRationale: Anchor: 'dead wood' — bowling slang for pins left lying in the lane after a strike, which must be cleared. Counter to Brunswick (active TM in bowling equipment). Deadwood is a trade-slang noun the brand owns plainly.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern bowling has shifted from sport-leagues toward hospitality-led venues — sixteen lanes, a kitchen, a long bar, a DJ booth. The opening is for a brand that names the room in trade language rather than entertainment-park language.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Lucky Strike (luckystrikeent.com) plays the modern-hospitality peer. Pinstripes (pinstripes.com) holds the bowling-bistro middle. Bowlero (bowlero.com) is the at-scale reference. We sit as a trade-named modern lanes brand.
Modern.positioningStatement: Deadwood Lanes is a modern bowling and bar venue named for the trade-slang noun for pins left in the lane.

targetAudience.primary: Adults 25-40 booking a Friday-night group of six to twelve, expecting food and drinks alongside the lanes.
behaviors: Book lanes online two weeks ahead

dos: Publish the lane price and the food menu side by side
Name the bartender on the staff page
donts: Photograph kids' birthday parties as the hero shot

Modern.logoDirection: Wordmark: DEADWOOD LANES set in a confident grotesk, two lines stacked. Small mark: a single pin laid on its side — the dead-wood silhouette — used on the lane-marker plaques.

typography.primary: Söhne for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Söhne Mono for lane prices and times
typography.rationale: One grotesk family plus its mono — the lane-board register.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Anchor: Plymouth Hoe — where Sir Francis Drake is said to have insisted on finishing his game of bowls in 1588 before sailing to meet the Spanish Armada. Counter to Drake's Green (uses a surname that may read as a real firm). The Hoe Club uses the geographic place plainly as a private-club frame.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury bowling is a thin category — private clubs with lawn bowls greens, private-event indoor lanes, and a small number of heritage hotel rooms. The buyer is a member or a private-events client.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: The All England Lawn Tennis Club (wimbledon.com) plays the private-club register peer. The Royal Automobile Club (royalautomobileclub.co.uk) holds the heritage-club reference. We sit as a private bowling club in the Hoe lineage.
Luxury.positioningStatement: The Hoe Club is a private bowling club in the lineage of the 1588 Plymouth Hoe game, offering lawn and indoor lanes to members.

targetAudience.primary: Members of long-standing London and provincial clubs interested in a quieter additional membership for bowls and lanes.
behaviors: Book the green for member events

Luxury.logoDirection: Wordmark: THE HOE CLUB set in a refined English serif, three lines centered. A hallmark — a single wood bowl with a small jack — used on the club crest and the member's tie.

typography.primary: Caslon for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Garamond Premier Pro for body and member letters
typography.rationale: Two classical English serifs — the private-club register.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the bowling pin, the central object of the trade. Counter to Roll (verb-as-noun, harder to register in this category) and Lane 7 (numeric, too generic). The full stop closes the wordmark as a single beat.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal bowling brands compete on rate clarity, lane availability, and zero entertainment-park theater. The opening is for a single-word venue named for the pin itself.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most bowling venues lean on entertainment-park branding. The Gutter (thegutterbrooklyn.com) plays the considered-minimal peer. Brooklyn Bowl (brooklynbowl.com) holds the venue-cool middle. We sit as the punctuated single-word minimal option.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Pin. is a minimal bowling venue named for the object — one rate card, ten pins, no theater.

targetAudience.primary: Adults 25-40 wanting to bowl with two friends after work without the family-entertainment overlay.
behaviors: Book the lane the same day
Pay by the hour, flat rate

dos: Publish the hourly rate on the home page
Show the lane, not the bar
Confirm the booking in one line

Minimal.logoDirection: Wordmark: PIN. set very large in a clean modern sans, three letters and a full stop. No symbol.

typography.primary: ABC Diatype for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: ABC Diatype Mono for the rate card
typography.rationale: Clean Diatype with its mono — the single-rate register.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Anchor: 'lanes' as the trade noun for a bowling venue, paired with a multi-site corporate suffix. Counter to Brunswick (active TM in bowling equipment) and Candlepin Holdings (limits the brand to a New England regional variant). National Lanes Co. reads as a multi-site operator in plain trade language.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate bowling operators run twenty to sixty venues with shared booking systems, supply contracts, and corporate-events programs. The category sits between independent venues and the at-scale national chains.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Bowlero (bowlero.com) plays the at-scale peer. AMF (amf.com) holds the heritage-chain middle. Pinstripes (pinstripes.com) is the bistro-format reference. We sit as a regional multi-site operator in the National Lanes Co. register.
Corporate.positioningStatement: National Lanes Co. is a regional bowling-venue operator running multiple lanes under shared operations, booking, and corporate-events programs.

targetAudience.primary: Corporate-events buyers, regional-venue investors, and franchise partners across mid-sized markets.

dos: Lead with venue footprint and capacity
Speak to corporate buyers and partners
donts: Run consumer-facing entertainment marketing at the parent level
Photograph individual parties as the hero shot

Corporate.logoDirection: Wordmark: NATIONAL LANES CO. set in an institutional serif, three lines centered. A small mark — a single bowling pin in silhouette — used on the contract cover.

typography.rationale: A reading serif plus a clean grotesk — the multi-venue operator register.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the gutter (the trough beside the lane, the trade word for a failed roll) and the glory (the strike). Counter to Sparehouse (coinage that loses the trade reference) and The Dead-Wood Tavern (closer to deadwood-modern). Gutter & Glory is the creative dichotomy paired-noun that lives on a neon sign.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative bowling venues compete on personality, neon, and a kitchen with a point of view. The opening is for a brand that names both outcomes plainly and runs the room as a bar with lanes.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Brooklyn Bowl (brooklynbowl.com) plays the venue-cool peer. The Gutter (thegutterbrooklyn.com) holds the dive-bowling middle. Highland Park Bowl (highlandparkbowl.com) is the heritage-revival reference. We sit as a paired-noun creative venue.
Creative.positioningStatement: Gutter & Glory is a creative bowling and bar venue named for both possible outcomes of a roll.

targetAudience.primary: Adults 25-40 looking for a night with friends that lands somewhere between a bar and a bowling alley.
behaviors: Order at the bar before the lane

dos: Name both the gutter and the strike on the scoreboard
Write the menu in the bartender's voice
Use neon as the brand's loudest visual

Creative.logoDirection: Wordmark: GUTTER & GLORY set in a punchy display serif, two lines, the ampersand drawn as a neon tube. Small mark: a single lit pin used as the venue stamp.

typography.primary: Druk for the wordmark and neon signage
typography.rationale: A display serif for the neon plus a clean grotesk for body — the bowling-bar register.
